reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a quasi-periodic pulse-train with a robust period of ~98 points (confirmed by catalog window_cycles and visual cycle counts). Each cycle consists of a sharp, near-vertical rise (~1–2 points) from a stable baseline near -1.0 to a narrow peak (duration ~3–5 points), followed by a smooth, monotonic exponential-like decay over ~60–70 points back toward baseline. Peaks are symmetric or slightly right-skewed, with robust-standardized amplitudes ranging 2.4–3.8 (90th percentile), and troughs consistently near -1.0. Baseline stability is high: after decay, the signal remains flat for ~20–30 points before the next rise. Noise is low—roughness metrics (0.025±0.008) indicate minimal high-frequency jitter. Minor trend variation exists across candidates (slope_per_point from -0.001 to +0.009), but all remain effectively stationary over single-cycle windows; long-term drift is negligible within analysis windows. Amplitude and decay rate show acceptable inter-cycle variation, but the core morphology—sharp onset, single dominant peak per cycle, slow decay, flat trough—is invariant across reliable candidates. Contamination risk arises only if a candidate lacks this pulse structure or shows multiple peaks/troughs per cycle.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 3 (5P) for queries with ≥3 cycles due to highest reliability and morphological consistency. Use reference 0 (1P) for single-pulse queries or when only short windows are available. Reference 1 is a robust fallback for 3-cycle queries; avoid reference 2 unless query shows similarly elevated amplitude and baseline shift—its lower reliability suggests it may reflect transient non-normal behavior.
uncertainties: Exact peak width tolerance (3–5 points) not quantified; minor variations may be normal

No ground-truth labels prevent confirmation of whether ref 2's double-rise is anomalous or natural variation
